findings.first_frame: 8.4s reads immediately: back view of a hooded figure and a small dark dog walking away from camera through pines/oaks, dappled sun on dry grass, no flare yet. Clean start.
findings.motion: Handheld follow shot, continuous walking for the whole 2.7s. Lens flare enters top-right at ~9.6s, peaks 10.0-10.4s (pink-white wash over roughly the right 40% of frame, figure and dog stay legible on the left), fades by 11.0s. That arc is the 'sunlight flickering through leaves' beat and it sits inside the cut rather than being clipped by it.
findings.faces: Back of head / hood only from 0s to 21.8s; the subject never turns. Dog is a small mid-ground shape, no face read.
findings.acting: Natural walk, no camera acknowledgement, no performance.
findings.tone: Already a faded, low-saturation, warm-grey film grade; needs little or no desaturation. The flare has a magenta tint, which is the only color that leans toward 'popping', but it stays hazy and filmic rather than a hard rainbow blob (unlike the 0-3s section of the same clip, which has a saturated pink flare circle and should not be used). Weaknesses: (1) forest floor, not a paved tree-lined sidewalk; (2) a dog walks alongside, which the brief did not ask for; (3) subject is about a quarter frame tall, so it reads as 'following someone' more than pure POV. All three are deviations of setting, not rule violations.
findings.framing: 16:9 1080p, 23.976fps; horizontal, so no center-crop needed. If the dog is unwanted, a ~1.25x center push-in keeps the figure and trims the dog toward the frame edge, but it is small enough to leave as is.
